name: Rhodes
title: Rhodes Ship Gauging | UTM for Ferries, Cruise & Island Cargo
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Rhodes for Dodecanese ferries, cruise ships, fuel tankers and coastal cargo: deck, tank and piping gauging.
h1: Rhodes: Thickness Gauging for Dodecanese Ferries and Island Shipping
intro: Rhodes is the hub of the Dodecanese, a few hours from the Turkish coast, with ferries, cruise ships, island supply vessels and fuel tankers using its harbours. Many of the ships that call have fixed timetables and short layovers. A team travels from India to the vessel, and gauging is fitted to the port call or to the winter break when island services slow down.

highlights.p: Island ferries and fast craft run to published schedules, so layovers are short and predictable. We agree a priority list of spaces with the superintendent and work to the timetable rather than against it.
Passenger traffic falls sharply after the summer, and ships that were in daily service become available for tank, void and vehicle deck gauging that cannot be fitted into a season of daily sailings.
Rhodes lies close to Marmaris and Fethiye, and ships often move between the two sides. Where visas and dates allow, one mobilisation can be planned around calls in both countries.

p: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands, lying off the south-west coast of Turkey at the eastern edge of the Aegean. The island's main harbour, Mandraki, is small and best known for yachts and excursion boats, while the commercial port next to it takes ferries, cruise ships and cargo. Rhodes Port Authority and the Hellenic Coast Guard administer the harbours, and a second, smaller harbour at Kolona and other facilities around the island serve fishing and local craft. The geography makes Rhodes a transport node for the whole chain, with services radiating to Kos, Kalymnos, Symi, Karpathos and beyond.

The ships that call are varied. Conventional ferries and fast craft link the Dodecanese with Piraeus and with each other, cruise ships call through the season and often anchor off the harbour in calm weather, and general cargo ships deliver building materials, supplies and consumer goods for the island and its neighbours. Fuel arrives by coastal product tanker, and some ships on the Greece-Turkey crossing use the port as an intermediate call. Much of the tonnage is coastal or short-sea, and a significant share is older: ships that have worked island routes for many years show wear on vehicle decks, ramps, weather decks and the boundaries of ballast tanks.

Rhodes is more exposed to weather than the north coast of Crete. Summer afternoon winds can complicate berthing, and winter storms from the south-west sometimes close the harbour for hours at a time. Because of that, work that needs calm water, such as anchorage gauging or launch transfers, is planned with margin. In midwinter, when services are reduced and some ships are laid up, a fuller condition programme is realistic. Island operators often schedule the biggest jobs for those months, so Rhodes sees much of its gauging between November and March.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged around Rhodes
p: In the commercial port, gauging is done alongside at the ferry and cargo quays. A ferry or cargo ship in port for a day offers accessible plating, vehicle decks, ramps, hatch covers and any tanks the crew has prepared. Product tankers delivering fuel are limited to deck, deck piping and ballast spaces and work within the terminal's permit rules. Cruise ships are usually on tight turnarounds, so readings concentrate on accessible deck and void spaces that the hotel operation does not block.

There is no large drydock on Rhodes. Ships needing hull steel work normally go to the Athens repair zones, to a yard in the Aegean or to Turkey, where yards at Marmaris and elsewhere along the coast serve yachts and smaller commercial ships. That means gauging on Rhodes is again a preparation step: measured readings help the technical manager set a steel estimate, compare yard offers and decide whether a repair can wait. For ships laid up in the harbour or at an anchorage during the winter, a longer programme can be planned over several days.
list: Commercial port ferry quays — vehicle deck, ramp, weather deck and ballast tank readings on island ferries and fast craft
Cargo quays — hatch cover, coaming and hold gauging on general cargo ships during discharge
Fuel berth — deck, deck piping and ballast tank readings on product tankers within terminal rules
Cruise berths and anchorage off the harbour — deck and void space gauging during turnaround calls
Winter lay-up berths — extended programmes on ships idle between seasons

context.h: Port state control and island regulation
p: Port state control at Rhodes falls under the Paris MoU and is carried out by the Hellenic Coast Guard, which also oversees passenger ship certification for the island services. Domestic ferries are surveyed regularly, so owners keep close watch on steel wastage in vehicle decks and ballast tanks. The Mediterranean emission control area for sulphur, in force from 1 May 2025, covers the Dodecanese. Shipping has been inside EU ETS since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, and both apply to island voyages as well as longer routes.

Rhodes sits near Turkish waters, which adds some practical points. Ships that cross between the two countries may be managed from either side, and a gauging scope agreed in one place may need to be carried out in the other. Where that happens, we need to know which technicians will cross and what visas each needs before the dates are set. For ships calling at EU ports an Inventory of Hazardous Materials must be on board, and changes of ownership or management on the island routes sometimes prompt a condition check outside the usual survey cycle.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Rhodes
jobs.p: Rhodes jobs tend to be built around the island operator's timetable. The superintendent names the spaces and the days available, we confirm what can be made safe by the crew in time, and the readings are reported by area as each is finished so the next step can be decided while the ship is still in port.
list: Vehicle deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on a Dodecanese ferry during winter lay-up, supporting the refit steel estimate.
Hatch cover and coaming readings on a general cargo ship delivering building materials to the island.
Deck plating and deck piping readings on a coastal product tanker alongside the fuel berth before vetting.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on an older ro-pax ship at the quay, with the buyer's superintendent attending.
Scrubber overboard piping inspection on a cruise ship during a turnaround call, after a discharge flange was found weeping.

logistics: The team flies into Rhodes International Airport Diagoras, usually through Athens, and travels by road to the harbour; the airport is a short drive from the town. Port passes, launch boarding for ships at anchor and any terminal permits are organised by the ship's agent from the crew list and equipment details we send ahead. Every technician needs a Schengen visa issued in India, because Greece applies the Schengen rules. For work that also covers a Turkish port we check that country's separate entry requirement at enquiry. Telling us the winter refit dates early helps visa planning.

faqs.q: Can a ferry be gauged during a Rhodes layover?
faqs.a: To a degree. A short layover usually allows deck, ramp and accessible plating readings, but tank entry needs spaces ventilated, tested and certified in advance. For ballast tanks and voids, the winter break is a far more realistic window, and we plan that programme with the superintendent well ahead.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock on Rhodes for steel renewal?
faqs.a: No large drydock is available on the island. Ships needing hull steel work normally go to Athens-area yards, to an Aegean yard or to the Turkish coast. Gauging here is best used to prepare: measured readings let you compare yard offers and order plate before the ship leaves Rhodes.

faqs.q: How does the weather affect work at Rhodes?
faqs.a: Strong summer winds and winter storms can delay berthing and launch transfers. Alongside work in the harbour is usually less affected, but anchorage jobs need margin. We leave slack in the schedule and keep the superintendent informed whenever the master or the agent changes the plan for weather.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover Rhodes and a Turkish port?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Marmaris and Fethiye are close, but Turkey needs its own entry permission separate from the Schengen visa. If both are in the plan, tell us when scoping so we can check requirements for each technician and fit the dates for both ships.

faqs.q: What can be gauged on a cruise ship in port?
faqs.a: Accessible deck, void and some tank spaces, depending on the turnaround and the hotel operation. We agree a short priority list with the technical manager and avoid areas that guests or catering use. Longer programmes belong in refit or lay-up, when more spaces can be opened safely.
